text:
[RFCS.2.3] **An unknown atom's disposition is fixed by its field number's
band, and skip is one of three answers.** The bands and their dispositions are
[RFCS.16.2]'s.

This is why every **additive** atom is allocated in the skip band — a new
atom type is then added without breaking existing readers, because a reader
that does not know it walks past it via the length prefix and replays
bit-identically.

Skip is **not** unconditional. An unknown atom in an inject band is exactly
the silently-dropped input the reject bands exist to catch ([RFCS.16.3],
[RFCS.18.8]): it is a fact the writer asserted and this reader cannot
represent.
